answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can submit one bid per hour. Whether agents sell ivory chess sets or arrange bridge repairs after a gale, the same limit applies. Creating 10,000 identities therefore ties up $1 million: new names alone buy no extra bidding capacity. The defense makes influence scale with committed capital, imposing a financing cost even if every bond is eventually returned.
